title: Roentgen and C/kg: Radiation Exposure Units
h1: Radiation exposure units — roentgen and C/kg
description: 1 R = 2.58 × 10⁻⁴ C/kg. Exposure measures ionisation in air, distinct from absorbed dose. Legacy R survives in older radiography and civil defence surveys.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

reviewer.name: Turbo Unit Converter editorial review
reviewer.credential: verified against NIST SP 811 and category-specific ISO references

hero: Exposure is not dose. It's ionisation of air per mass. Historical but still turns up on Geiger counters.
body: Exposure predates the modern absorbed-dose framework. It measures how much air a radiation field ionises, and it applies only to photons in air.

> 1 R (roentgen) = 2.58 × 10⁻⁴ C/kg (of air)
> 1 C/kg = 3876 R
> For diagnostic X-rays in soft tissue: 1 R ≈ 0.87 rad ≈ 8.7 mGy

Roentgen: legacy US radiography, older civil-defence Geiger counters, some geology field surveys. C/kg: SI standard, industrial radiation protection metrology. Modern practice mostly reports air kerma (Gy) instead of exposure.

Old CD V-717 civil-defence meter reads 5 R/h. Modern equivalent air kerma rate: 5 × 8.76 mGy/R ≈ 44 mGy/h. Effective dose rate ≈ 44 mSv/h (for photons). Six minutes exposure at this rate delivers annual worker limit.
R is exposure, not dose. For photons in tissue, 1 R ≈ 1 rad. Modern practice reports Gy directly.

faqs.q: Is R the same as rem?
faqs.a: For gamma and X-rays in tissue, numerically close (1 R ≈ 0.87 rem). Not for other radiation types.

faqs.q: Do modern meters read in R?
faqs.a: Rarely — most report µSv/h or nGy/h. R is legacy.
